chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Aslam al-Jabali, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a woman who had a husband, committed zina, became pregnant, and when she gave birth, secretly killed her child. He said: “She is to be lashed one hundred times for killing her child, and she is to be stoned because she is muhsanah.”

He said: And I asked him about a woman without a husband who committed zina, became pregnant, and when she gave birth, secretly killed her child. He said: “She is to be lashed one hundred times because she committed zina, and she is to be lashed one hundred times because she killed her child.”

key_terms.ذَاتِ بَعْلٍ: a woman who has a husband
key_terms.مُحْصَنَةٌ: legally protected through marriage, making the hadd of stoning applicable in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a woman who commits zina and then secretly kills her newborn child?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning two cases: a married woman and an unmarried woman who commit zina, become pregnant, and then secretly kill the child after birth. The ruling distinguishes between the punishment for zina based on marital status, while also assigning a separate punishment for the killing of the child.
